clues.title: Plate: Hungary uses long white standard European licence plates
text: Hungary uses **long white** standard European licence plates. Taxi licence plates are **yellow.**
In July of 2022, Hungary switched to this new character format, which contains the coat of arms.
NOTE: Newer electric vehicles have green plates.

clues.title: Bollard: Hungarian bollards are black-and-white
text: Hungarian bollards are black-and-white, wedge-shaped, and typically have a **red** reflector at the front, and a white reflector at the back. [Blue reflectors](https://www.google.com/maps/@47.826971,20.8472466,3a,15y,282.66h,79.6t/data=!3m6!1e1!3m4!1s9lVB-fYRUINpTrMAYWvYZg!2e0!7i16384!8i8192) are also somewhat common.

NOTE: [Croatian bollards](https://www.google.se/maps/@44.9117293,15.1630293,3a,17.5y,144.5h,72.84t/data=!3m6!1e1!3m4!1sQHfQsXnyjPhm0AakdfHr0A!2e0!7i16384!8i8192) are very similar. They do, however, typically have the reflector closer to the top, and appear somewhat [thinner](https://www.google.se/maps/@44.9122903,15.1621345,3a,48.7y,222.73h,52.12t/data=!3m6!1e1!3m4!1sbWEK8Fssx79YL61MpgzMqg!2e0!7i16384!8i8192) than in Hungary.

clues.title: Pole: The most common type of utility pole in Hungary is a…
text: The most common type of utility pole in Hungary is a **concrete holey pole**, with relatively thin holes going all the way down to the ground. Wooden poles are also somewhat common.

NOTE: In eastern Europe, Poland and Romania also commonly use holey poles. [Polish holey poles](https://www.google.com/maps/@49.9926761,18.7114721,3a,55.1y,130.81h,98.23t/data=!3m6!1e1!3m4!1sHtPKStzKxeiHUY1s-iNu-w!2e0!7i16384!8i8192) typically do not have holes down by the ground, and tend to be relatively thin. [Romanian holey poles](https://goo.gl/maps/QyJwGvUuzdnJLVBv5) normally either have much wider, or much taller holes.

clues.title: Chevron: Hungarian chevrons are white on red
text: Hungarian chevrons are **white on red**.

[Black-and-white](https://www.google.com/maps/@47.2517674,16.9392096,3a,37.6y,261.49h,65.38t/data=!3m7!1e1!3m5!1s_Vx5ThXqoem-sKrW96OMFw!2e0!5s20111101T000000!7i13312!8i6656) chevrons may also be seen, but are considerably less common.

clues.title: Language: The Hungarian language has a unique look
text: The **Hungarian language** has a unique look, with a very large number of [acute accents](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acute_accent), [umlauts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umlaut_(diacritic)) over o’s, and long words. The letters "Ő" and "Ű", with double acute accents, are unique to the language.
NOTE: Hungarian is also spoken in some parts of neighbouring countries: notably there are large Hungarian-speaking communities in central Romania and southern Slovakia.

clues.title: Street sign: Hungarian street names typically end with the word “utca”
text: Hungarian street names typically end with the word “**utca**”. The word “út” is also used for bigger roads. These two words are unique to Hungarian, and translate to “street.”

clues.title: These green kilometre markers can be seen along most…
text: These **green kilometre markers** can be seen along most Hungarian roads.
On highways, the numbers correspond to the ones seen on the map in small yellow boxes near exits.

clues.title: Sign: Hungarian sign posts commonly appear to be abnormally tall
text: Hungarian sign posts commonly appear to be **abnormally tall**, often taller than the Street View camera.

clues.title: Sign: Hungarian signs are usually bolted to the sign post using…
text: Hungarian signs are usually bolted to the sign post using **four bolts**, going through the sign, in the shape of a tall rectangle.
NOTE: This is not common in any other Eastern European countries.

clues.title: Pedestrian sign: Hungarian pedestrian crossing signs have five stripes
text: Hungarian pedestrian crossing signs have **five stripes**. The person is wearing a **belt**. There is also a second, less common, type with four stripes and the person holding a bag.
The belt is located noticeably **low** on the person’s body, almost as if the person is sagging his pants. This is unique to Hungary.
NOTE: Among neighbouring countries, Croatia and Slovakia also have five stripes and a belt.

clues.title: Route marker: Apart from European highways
text: Apart from European highways, there are two types of numbered roads in Hungary; roads marked with **green signs**, and highways beginning with the letter ‘**M**’, marked with **blue signs**. These road numbers are contained within a small shield shape on the sign.

clues.title: Direction sign: Most directional signs are green
text: Most directional signs are green, having a white inner border and a green outer border. Directional signs on M-numbered highways are blue, having a white inner border and a blue outer border.

clues.title: Google car: It is somewhat common to see a small
text: It is somewhat common to see a small, grey flag on the antenna of Generation 3 Google cars in Hungary.
NOTE: This is also seen in the Czech Republic, Slovakia, Romania and Bulgaria.

clues.title: Google car: A white generation 4 Google car can also rarely be found in…
text: A white generation 4 Google car can also rarely be found in Hungary.
NOTE: It can also be found in other European countries.

clues.title: Google car: A black generation 4 car that will never have an antenna…
text: A black generation 4 car that will never have an antenna can be found in Hungary.
NOTE: A black car can be found in many European countries, though it will often have an antenna visible.

clues.title: Google car: The majority of Generation 3 coverage in Hungary was taken…
text: The majority of Generation 3 coverage in Hungary was taken **during winter**, resulting in very grey, dead looking coverage.
NOTE: This is also common in the Czech Republic and Bulgaria.

clues.title: Architecture: Hungarian houses are typically made of stone
text: Hungarian houses are typically made of stone, painted in a light colour and almost always with **red tiled roofs**. Suburban houses are typically only one storeyed, while more central houses may be taller. Houses in town and city centres are often fairly old but well-kept.

clues.title: Road line: While Hungarian road lines are all-white
text: While Hungarian road lines are all-white, lines on **bicycle lanes** are typically **yellow**.

clues.title: Hungarian phone numbers consist of either 8 or 10 digits
text: Hungarian phone numbers consist of either 8 or 10 digits. If the number has 8 digits, the first and second digit is the **area code**. And if the number has 10 digits, the third and fourth digit is the area code. The only exception is Budapest, where only the first or third digit, being a 1, respectively is the area code.
NOTE: Area codes whose second digit is 0 or 1 are not region specific.

clues.title: The first digit of Hungarian numbered roads are ordered in…
text: The first digit of Hungarian **numbered roads** are ordered in a circle, centred around Budapest. Remembering this system should make it quite easy to find any numbered road.

clues.title: Street sign: If you see a street sign with a thick metal frame around it
text: If you see a street sign with a **thick metal frame** around it, you are very likely to be in the **western** parts of the country.

clues.title: Pole: If you see a blue or green street sign shaped like an arrow
text: If you see a **blue** or **green** street sign shaped like an **arrow**, attached to a utility pole or street light, you are likely to be in the county of Szabolcs-Szatmár-Bereg.

NOTE: Blue arrow-shaped street signs can also be found in [Dunakeszi](https://www.google.com/maps/@47.6290186,19.1549932,3a,29.7y,151.87h,90.55t/data=!3m6!1e1!3m4!1se_1iRMK0jnxi0R13E9x-8A!2e0!7i16384!8i8192), north of Budapest. However, those are attached to blue sign posts.

clues.title: Landscape: While the southeastern parts of Hungary are extremely flat
text: While the southeastern parts of Hungary are extremely flat, with almost no noticeable hills, the northern and western parts mainly consist of **forested hills and mountains**. The tallest mountains are found in the north, while the southwestern mountains are generally slightly lower.

clues.title: Lake Balaton is one of the largest lakes on mainland Europe
text: Lake Balaton is one of the largest lakes on mainland Europe, and the **only large lake** visible on street view in Hungary. The area surrounding the lake is moderately hilly, fairly built up and a big tourist destination, with a much higher density of small hotels than almost anywhere else in the country.

clues.title: Unlike most of the Hungarian plains
text: Unlike most of the Hungarian plains, which is almost entirely cultivated land, the Puszta, centred around Hortobágy National Park, mainly consists of barren and wet, natural grasslands.

clues.title: Language: Hungarian
text: Hungarian is a Ugric language that is unrelated to all its surrounding languages. It has a unique look, with a large number of acute accents (**Á, É, Í, Ó, Ú**), umlauts (**Ö, Ü**), and long words. The letters **Ő** and **Ű**, with **double** acute accents, are unique to the language.
The Hungarian name for street is **utca**. The word **út** is also used for bigger roads. No other language shares this name.
NOTE: Hungarian is widely spoken is parts of neighboring countries, notably Romania and Slovakia.
